capitals.name: Beirut
capitals.note: The Mandate page names Beirut as capital of the State of Greater Lebanon (and Damascus, Aleppo, Latakia and As-Suwayda as capitals of the other states of the mandate); it does not name the seat of the High Commissioner, so Beirut is the researcher's reading of the page.

keyframe_review.note: 1920-1921, 210,022 km2: the mandate lands plus a strip in southern Turkey (28 cells, about 7,000 km2, with 3 in Iraq and 2 in Jordan) that the 1922 shape no longer has. The Ankara page says the border was fixed on 20 October 1921 'immediately south of Payas', then to the Baghdad Railway at Al-Rai and along the track to Nusaybin, and that France 'ceded large areas to Turkey' (Adana, Osmaniye, Marash, Aintab, Kilis, Urfa, Mardin, Nusaybin, Cizre); the shape holds only the southern edge of that zone, so the French-occupied Cilicia belt is carried by an occupation event, not by this shape. The Mandate page gives no area (infobox figure absent), so no ratio could be taken. Adjusted after review: the 1920 shape holds the whole of Syria, but the Mandate page has Goybet 'captured Damascus with little resistance on 24 July 1920', so the Syrian interior is counted for the Arab Kingdom in 1920 and enters this state in 1921 (event 3).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the second year of Cliopatria's 1920-1921 shape, 210,022 km2, carried unchanged after the fall of Damascus. The strip north of the Ankara line leaves in January 1922 (events 5 and 6), the date of the 1922 shape.
1922-1925, 201,572 km2: the border south of the Ankara line (the Baghdad Railway to Nusaybin) as the 1921 agreement describes it; 28 cells in Turkey fewer than 1920. The Mandate page gives no area.

1926 only, 201,513 km2: one cell (250 km2) of the Syrian desert border differs from 1922 and returns in 1927; read as drawing noise. The page records no territorial change in 1926 (Greater Lebanon became the Lebanese Republic on 23 May 1926 within the mandate).
1927-1931, 201,572 km2, identical to 1922. The Great Syrian Revolt of these years is not on the page opened; no border moved.

1932-1935, 201,259 km2: three cells (about 750 km2, two in Syria and one in Lebanon, 32.4-33.9 N) fewer than 1927; no page opened dates a frontier change, so read as drawing noise. The Mandate page records the Alawite State renamed on 22 September 1930 'Independent Government of Latakia' and Jabal Druze autonomous from 24 October 1922, both inside the shape.

correction.text: years only: holds 1936-1937 unchanged, Sanjak of Alexandretta included (under a special statute from November 1937); 1938 is described by the new keyframe french-mandate-for-syria-and-lebanon_1938

keyframe_review.note: 1936-1938 in Cliopatria, 200,893 km2, with 4 cells (1,000 km2) of the Iraqi border differing from 1932 (read as noise). The Hatay page dates the Hatay State to 2 September 1938, so 1938 needs its own shape; the Alawite State and Jabal Druze joined the State of Syria in 1936 ('the Alawite state finally joined the Syrian Republic on 5 December 1936'), which moved no outer border.

correction.text: the 1936 shape without the Sanjak of Alexandretta: 'On 2 September 1938, the sanjak assembly proclaimed the Sanjak of Alexandretta as the Hatay State'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria keeps the sanjak in the mandate shape through 1938 and removes it in 1939, but the page puts the Hatay State in September 1938 (joint French and Turkish military supervision) and the annexation by Turkey on 23 July 1939. The cut is dated to the event year as the project's yearly step requires.

1939 only, 195,967 km2: the 1936 shape without Hatay (17 cells in Turkey, 2 in Syria, about 4,750 km2). The Hatay page: 'By 23 July 1939, the last vestiges of the French Mandate authorities had left Antakya, and the territory was fully annexed by Turkey.' Mandate page gives no area.

1940-1942, 195,967 km2, identical to 1939. The 1941 campaign (8 June to 14 July 1941, Vichy against the British Empire and Free French) changed who administered the mandate, not its outline: 'Syria and Lebanon taken over by Free France'.
1943 only, 195,942 km2, with Lebanon. 'Lebanon became an independent state on 22 November 1943', so the Lebanese part holds only to November; Cliopatria drops Lebanon from 1944.

1944 only, 186,232 km2: Syria alone (29 Lebanese cells, 2 in Israel and 1 in Syria fewer than 1943; 2 Syrian cells added). The Levant Crisis page: 'it was not until 1 January 1944 that it was recognised as an independent republic', but French troops stayed until April 1946, so the shape is kept as the mandate in practice; a status question (vassal tint) for the reviewer.

1945 only, 186,885 km2 (six cells more than 1944 on the Iraqi and Jordanian edges, read as noise). The May-July 1945 Levant Crisis: French troops shelled Damascus on 29 May and on 31 May Churchill asked de Gaulle to 'order French troops to cease fire and withdraw to their barracks'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends this row in 1945 and starts the Second Syrian Republic in 1946; the page says 'Syria became fully independent on 17 April 1946', so the mandate's last months are drawn on the 1945 shape and the Second Syrian Republic dossier takes over (it may duplicate the year).

region.text: Cilicia and the Aintab-Urfa-Mardin belt: 'the French controlled the rest of Ottoman Syria (including Lebanon, Alexandretta and portions of Cilicia)'

ledger.note: April 1920: the mandate holds the French-occupied Cilician belt. The Mandate page says 'the French controlled the rest of Ottoman Syria (including Lebanon, Alexandretta and portions of Cilicia)' and names Gouraud 'high commissioner in Syria and Cilicia' (1919 section). The Franco-Turkish War page (second page, re-read 2026-10-25) dates the occupation itself earlier: 'The first landing took place on 17 November 1918 at Mersin' (infobox of the war: 7 December 1918 - 20 October 1921), and Antep, Marash and Urfa passed 'from British troops' at the end of 1919. Those months precede this state's life (April 1920), so the occupation enters the ledger at the mandate's founding; the earlier months belong to french-third-republic, and the ottoman-empire dossier's Cilicia loss (1919, counterpart french-third-republic) should read 1918-11. The Turkish side is the Grand National Assembly at Ankara (Ottoman Empire row used as the owner of record).

minus.text: the Arab Kingdom of Syria's land inside Syria: Damascus and the Syrian interior without the Latakia and Tartus coast (the arab-kingdom-of-syria dossier's region, restricted to Syria)

region.text: the mandate zone without the Arab Kingdom's interior: Lebanon, the Syrian coast (Latakia, Tartus), Alexandretta and the Cilician strip, 'granted France the mandate of Syria (including Lebanon)'; the interior of Syria enters with the fall of Damascus in July 1920

ledger.note: 1920: the Allies give France the mandate for Syria and Lebanon. 'On 25 April, the Supreme Inter-Allied Council ... granted France the mandate of Syria (including Lebanon)' (the page's 1920 section; the League of Nations assigned it on 29 September 1923 and the text was written 'on 24 July 1922'). Cliopatria's shape starts in 1920. The region excludes the interior of Syria, which Faisal's Arab Kingdom of Syria still holds until the French take Damascus on 24 July 1920 (event 3; arab-kingdom-of-syria dissolves in July 1920). Counterpart: the land is Ottoman de jure, but the ottoman-empire dossier records the loss of Syria and Lebanon in October 1918 to british-colonial-empire, and the Mandate page has the French in the Lebanese coastal region from 8 October 1918 where they 'replaced the British troops there'; the occupying administration is therefore the counterpart. On 1 September 1920 'General Gouraud publicly proclaimed the creation of the State of Greater Lebanon', capital Beirut; the mandate also held the States of Damascus, Aleppo, the Alawite State and Jabal Druze, none a separate sovereign.

region.text: the road to Damascus at Maysaloun

ledger.note: July 1920: Gouraud attacks Faisal. 'On 14 July 1920, General Gouraud issued an ultimatum to Faisal'; the French 'won the battle [of Maysaloun] in less than a day'.

region.text: the Arab Kingdom of Syria's land inside Syria: Damascus and the Syrian interior without the Latakia and Tartus coast (the arab-kingdom-of-syria dossier's region, restricted to Syria)

ledger.note: 24 July 1920: France takes Damascus. Gouraud's forces 'captured Damascus with little resistance' on 24 July 1920; the page does not list the other cities, so the region is the researcher's reading: Syria without the Latakia and Tartus coast that event 1 already counts, which is the land the arab-kingdom-of-syria dossier loses in July 1920. The interior is counted once, here.

region.text: the road to Damascus at Maysaloun

ledger.note: 24 July 1920: the French win at Maysaloun 'in less than a day' and Gouraud's forces capture Damascus; the page records no further fighting of the war.

region.text: Adana, Osmaniye, Marash, Aintab, Kilis, Urfa, Mardin, Nusaybin and Jazirat ibn Umar (Cizre), the places the Ankara Agreement 'ceded to Turkey'

ledger.note: January 1922: France leaves the Cilician belt. Franco-Turkish War page: 'The French forces withdrew from the occupation zone in the first days of 1922', evacuation of Mersin and Dortyol from 3 January and 'completed on 7 January with the last troops leaving Osmaniye'. The Ankara Agreement of 20 October 1921, signed by Henry Franklin-Bouillon and Yusuf Kemal Bey, had 'ceded to Turkey' Adana, Osmaniye, Marash, Aintab, Kilis, Urfa, Mardin, Nusaybin and Cizre (Treaty of Ankara page); the first draft of this event used that date.

region.text: the strip north of the new border, 'immediately south of Payas' to the Baghdad Railway at Al-Rai and 'the railway track to Nusaybin'

ledger.note: January 1922: the strip north of the Ankara line passes to Turkey. The Ankara Agreement of 20 October 1921 fixed the border 'immediately south of Payas' to the Baghdad Railway and 'the railway track to Nusaybin' and France 'ceded large areas to Turkey' (Treaty of Ankara page); the Franco-Turkish War page puts the French evacuation in 'the first days of 1922' (completed 7 January), which agrees with Cliopatria's 1922 shape. The region is the difference between Cliopatria's 1920 and 1922 shapes (28 cells in Turkey).

region.text: the Sea of Galilee and the Yarmuk valley, which the 1922 commission amendments put in Palestine

ledger.note: 7 March 1923: the Franco-British frontier is settled. The Paulet-Newcombe page says the agreement was 'approved with some caveats by the French and British governments on 7 March 1923' and that the 1922 commission amendments moved the northern boundary north 'to include the entire Sea of Galilee and the Yarmuk valley', increasing Palestine's area; the 1920 convention had 'placed the bulk of the Golan Heights in the French sphere', and Banias stayed under the French mandate. The strip is small: Cliopatria's 1922-1925 mandate shape holds no Sea of Galilee cell (0 cells), so no keyframe changes; the region is the researcher's reading of the page's words.

region.text: Jabal al-Druze (As-Suwayda) and the Damascus countryside (Ghouta), where the rebels set up their National Provisional Government and fought for Damascus

ledger.note: 21 July 1925: the Druze win the battle of al-Kafr, the first fight of the Great Syrian Revolt that holds ground. The page gives the infobox span '1925-1927', Sultan al-Atrash's declaration of revolution on 23 August 1925 and says the Druze 'revolted in September 1925'; the Druze 'captured the fort at al-Suwayda' and rebels and nationalists set up a National Provisional Government there, with al-Atrash as president. Rebels assaulted Damascus (Hasan al-Kharrat), which was bombarded from the air, and al-Qawuqji led the Hama rising of 4-5 October 1925 and the Ghouta fighting. The month is the first dated battle; the page's own dates for the outbreak differ.

region.text: Jabal al-Druze (As-Suwayda) and the Damascus countryside (Ghouta), where the rebels set up their National Provisional Government and fought for Damascus

ledger.note: Late June 1927: the revolt ends. The page says the uprisings 'continued until late June 1927'; it also gives the defeat of the Druze as 'the spring of the following year' (1926) in one passage and as spring 1927 in others. Sultan al-Atrash went into exile in Transjordan; the infobox result is 'French victory'. No frontier changed.

region.text: the Sanjak of Alexandretta, 'proclaimed ... as the Hatay State'

ledger.note: 2 September 1938: the Sanjak of Alexandretta becomes the Hatay State. 'On 2 September 1938, the sanjak assembly proclaimed the Sanjak of Alexandretta as the Hatay State'; it 'lasted for one year under joint French and Turkish military supervision' and Turkey annexed it by 23 July 1939 (the Turkish dossier carries the gain).

region.text: Syria and Lebanon, the campaign's theatre

ledger.note: 8 June 1941: British, Commonwealth and Free French forces invade the Vichy-held mandate. 'Hostilities commenced on 8 June 1941.' British and Commonwealth forces 'carried out the invasion'.

region.text: Syria and Lebanon, the campaign's theatre

ledger.note: 14 July 1941: Vichy forces yield by the Armistice of Saint Jean d'Acre. 'At one minute past midnight on 12 July, a ceasefire came into effect'; the armistice 'was signed on 14 July at the Sidney Smith Barracks' outside Acre.

July 1941: the mandate passes from Vichy France to Free France. Infobox territorial change 'Syria and Lebanon taken over by Free France'; General Georges Catroux was put in charge. The outline of the mandate does not change.

region.text: Lebanon, which 'became an independent state on 22 November 1943'

ledger.note: 22 November 1943: Lebanon becomes independent. 'Lebanon became an independent state on 22 November 1943.' Cliopatria drops Lebanon from the mandate shape in 1944.

region.text: Damascus, shelled by French troops on 29 May 1945

ledger.note: 29 May 1945: French troops shell Damascus. 'On Beynet's command, General Oliva-Roget ordered his troops to begin shelling Damascus on May 29' and 'French troops stormed the Syrian parliament'; the infobox dates the crisis 19 May to 19 July 1945. Counterpart: the second-syrian-republic dossier opens in April 1946, so the Syrian state of 1945 is named as the reviewer suggests; the Levant Crisis page itself says 'Syria' (infobox belligerents 'United Kingdom; Syria' against France).

1945: the Levant Crisis ends. Churchill's 31 May message asked the French to 'cease fire and withdraw to their barracks'; the infobox gives 'British-Syrian victory' and 'French withdrawal from the Levant' with the end on 19 July 1945. Counterpart: the second-syrian-republic dossier opens in April 1946, so the Syrian state of 1945 is named as the reviewer suggests; the Levant Crisis page itself says 'Syria' (infobox belligerents 'United Kingdom; Syria' against France).

region.text: Syria, the last land of the mandate

ledger.note: 17 April 1946: the French mandate ends. 'Syria became fully independent on 17 April 1946' and 'The French evacuated the last of their troops in April of that year'.

wars.name: Franco-Syrian War
wars.outcome: French victory at Maysaloun in less than a day; Damascus taken on 24 July 1920 and the Arab Kingdom of Syria ended.
wars.note: Only the Mandate page was opened; it gives the ultimatum of 14 July and the capture of Damascus on 24 July 1920.

wars.name: Franco-Turkish War
wars.outcome: The Ankara Agreement of 20 October 1921 ended the war and France ceded Adana, Osmaniye, Marash, Aintab, Kilis, Urfa, Mardin, Nusaybin and Cizre to Turkey; the French forces withdrew from the occupation zone in the first days of 1922 (completed 7 January).
wars.note: Franco-Turkish War page, infobox '7 December 1918 - 20 October 1921'; 'The first landing took place on 17 November 1918 at Mersin'. The war began before this state's life (April 1920); the mandate administration took over the Cilician belt at its founding. The Turkish belligerent was the Ankara Government (Grand National Assembly), here the Ottoman Empire row.

wars.outcome: French victory: the uprisings 'continued until late June 1927'; Sultan al-Atrash went into exile in Transjordan and Shahbandar fled to Transjordan and then Egypt.
wars.note: Infobox '1925-1927', location 'State of Syria and Greater Lebanon'. The page's dates for the Druze defeat conflict (spring 1926 in one passage, spring 1927 in others); no frontier moved. The rebels' National Provisional Government at al-Suwayda has no dossier.

wars.name: Syria-Lebanon campaign
wars.outcome: Allied victory: ceasefire 12 July and the Armistice of Saint Jean d'Acre on 14 July 1941; Free France took over the administration of both territories.

wars.name: Levant Crisis
wars.outcome: British-Syrian victory; the British ordered the French to cease fire on 31 May 1945 and the French withdrew, the last troops leaving in April 1946.
wars.note: The infobox gives 19 May - 19 July 1945 and belligerents 'United Kingdom; Syria' against France; the Syrian state is named 'Syrian Republic (1930-1950)' because the second-syrian-republic dossier opens in April 1946.

certainty.note: Military occupation lines: the Cilician belt and the strip along the Turkish side were French-held (since the landing at Mersin on 17 November 1918) until the evacuation of the first days of January 1922 that followed the Ankara Agreement of 20 October 1921; the Damascus conquest of July 1920 is dated but its limits are not.

The Turkish frontier follows the 1921 agreement (the Baghdad Railway to Nusaybin); the Hatay cut of 1938-39 is dated. The desert frontiers with Iraq, Transjordan and Palestine are described on no page opened and are drawn as Cliopatria has them.

notes:
Wikidata Q139708 is shared with the Cliopatria row 'Lebanon' (1944..2024, slug lebanon): they are different states. The Mandate row is the French-administered Syria and Lebanon of 1920-1945 (this dossier, which ends with Syria in April 1946); 'Lebanon' is the independent republic that the lebanon dossier starts in November 1943. The Wikidata id was carried over from Cliopatria and probably belongs to one of them only.

Decisions: (1) start April 1920 (San Remo allotment, 'On 25 April' in the page's 1920 section; the League assigned the mandate on 29 September 1923, the page's infobox span '1923-1946'), end April 1946 against Cliopatria's 1945; the Second Syrian Republic dossier starts the same month, so 1946 may be drawn twice. (2) Lebanon leaves in November 1943 (lebanon dossier), Hatay in September 1938 (the hatay-state dossier was written by this batch), Cilicia and the Ankara strip in January 1922 (the evacuation after the Ankara Agreement of 20 October 1921). (3) type 'colony', family 'france' so the mandate takes a tint of the Third Republic's colour.

Not reached: the Franco-Syrian Treaty of 1936; the Syria-Iraq and Syria-Transjordan frontier agreements. Small cell changes in 1926, 1932, 1936 and 1945 (250-1,500 km2) are read as drawing noise. The Mandate page gives no infobox area, so no ratio against Cliopatria's 210,022 km2 could be taken. Gazetteer: 'Cilicia' is in regions.jsonl; the Turkish provinces are used for the Cilician belt.

Repair round (2026-10-25), after review: (1) the found event no longer takes the Syrian interior: its region is the 1920 shape minus Syria-without-the-coast (the Arab Kingdom's land), the July 1920 gain takes that land once, and the 1920 keyframe was split (_1920 without the interior, new _1921 with the full shape) so the interior is not drawn for both states in 1920. (2) The found counterpart is british-colonial-empire, the occupying administration the ottoman-empire dossier names for its October 1918 loss of Syria and Lebanon; the de jure Ottoman reading is kept in the predecessors. The ottoman-empire dossier still lacks a French Cilicia loss dated 1918-11 (it has 1919, counterpart french-third-republic) and the 1921-22 gain of the Ankara strip. (3) The Levant Crisis contest and war name 'Syrian Republic (1930-1950)' because second-syrian-republic opens in 1946; I note that the Levant Crisis page itself says only 'Syria'. (4) The Cilicia occupation was dated from the Franco-Turkish War page: landing 17 November 1918, infobox 7 December 1918 - 20 October 1921, withdrawal completed 7 January 1922; the occupation event stays at April 1920 (the mandate's founding) and the pre-1920 months belong to french-third-republic. The occupation end and the strip loss move from October 1921 to January 1922. (5) Added: the Great Syrian Revolt (war entry, contest 1925-07 to 1927-06 in Jabal Druze and the Damascus countryside against 'Syrian rebels (Great Syrian Revolt)', a name with no dossier) and the Paulet-Newcombe loss of 1923-03 (counterpart 'Mandatory Palestine', no dossier; Cliopatria's shape holds no Sea of Galilee cell, so nothing changes in the keyframes; the Golan bulk stayed with the mandate). Both new counterparts are listed for the additions batch.
